1.text:
"O believers! Honour your obligations" opens the passage by naming the people it speaks to and setting a command on them before anything is made lawful. The obligations are the bonds a person has confirmed, the covenants settled between a person and Allah and between one person and other people, and the word in the verse reaches the pledges a person has taken on, the promises made with His creation in sale transactions and in marriage, the treaties, and what Allah has made lawful or made unlawful, ordained and set limits for in the Qur'an, so everything after this in the passage sits inside the opening command to keep faith. The person addressed is free in the world to do whatever he likes, and yet by this call he admits the supremacy and Lordship of God and makes himself subject to regulation, and of his own he ties himself in the bondage of a vow, so honouring the obligations is the shape that submission takes in the matter of God or His subjects, and it is not acted out independently but stands by His commandments in all his dealings. Then "All grazing livestock has been made lawful to you" turns from what a person owes to what a person may eat, and the phrase names the grazing livestock, the plural of the word for the beasts of the flocks, camels, cattle and sheep and goats, taken to cover the eight kinds of domestic animals, so the lawful is broad here and it is stated before its edges. The edges come in the next phrase, "except what is hereby announced to you and hunting while on pilgrimage". "Indeed, Allah commands what He wills" closes the verse on the authority behind both halves, and what is announced to you is the specific cases that take some of these back out of the lawful, the verses after this naming carrion and the rest one by one. Hunting is the second exception, with game not being lawful to you when you are on pilgrimage, or in the Sacred Precinct, so one act can be lawful at one time and not lawful at another, and the verse marks which time is which. The closing phrase stands over all of it: He decrees whatever He desires in the way of making things lawful or otherwise, He makes lawful or unlawful what He wills whether a person is in a state of ritual consecration or not, and there can be no objection thereto, and no one can compel Him or object to His decision.

**What the call to fulfil your bonds includes.**

O you who believe fulfil your bonds the covenants confirmed between you and God and between you and other people. (Fulfill (your) obligations.) Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and others said that 'obligations' here means treaties. (O you who believe! Fulfill (your) obligations.) "Refers to the covenants, meaning, what Allah permitted, prohibited, ordained and set limits for in the Qur'an. This is what has been reported from Sayyidna Ibn Abbas Others say that here it means the contracts people enter into with each other, such as, the Contract of Marriage and the Contract of Buying and Selling. O you who believe in Allah, follow His Messenger and practice His laws, fulfil the firm promises of faith and practice that were made between you and your Creator.

**The pledges that are between you and Allah and between you and people.**

(O ye who believe! Fulfil your undertakings): '(O ye who believe! Fulfil your undertakings) fulfil the pledges that are between you and Allah or between you and other people; it is also said that this means: fulfil the obligations which have been made obligatory upon you and which you accepted on the Day of the Covenant and in this Book. Some say that it refers to the Covenant of Allah under which His created beings are bound to believe in and obey Him, or they refer to pledges Allah has taken from His created beings regarding His revealed injunctions of things lawful and unlawful. The vow is the same shape taken on one's own. Although he is free in the world to do whatever he likes, in spite of this, he admits the supremacy and Lordship of God and makes himself subject to regulation. Of his own he ties himself in the bondage of a vow. In the matter of God or His subjects he has taken it upon himself not to act independently but according to God’s commandments. Also, fulfil the promises made with His creation in sale transactions, marriage, etc.

**Which animals are made lawful, and what is excepted.**

Lawful to you is the beast of the flocks camels cattle and sheep and goats to eat after slaughtering them except that which is now being recited to you as forbidden in the verse below Forbidden to you are carrion…Q. 53; the exceptive clause here is a discontinuous one but may also be continuous; the forbidding concerns that which has succumbed to death and the like; game not being lawful to you when you are on pilgrimage hurum means muhrimūn; ghayra ‘not’ is in the accusative as it introduces a circumstantial qualifier referring to the subject of the pronoun lakum ‘to you’. The word, al-An am', used in the text is the plural form of na'am (grazing livestock). So, the meaning of the verse comes to be that eight kinds of domestic animals have been made lawful for you.' Under the discussion about the word, al- uqud', you have already read a little earlier that it includes all kinds of contracts. Allah has permitted for you, out of His mercy, livestock animals (camels, cattle, sheep and goats), except those the prohibition of which have been read to you and the land game that He has prohibited you from in the state of sanctity during the pilgrimage of Hajj or Umrah.

**What is recited to you as excepted during the pilgrimage, and the game of the hunt.**

(The beast of cattle is made lawful unto you (for food) you have a legal dispensation to eat of the meat of game such as wild oxen, wild camels and gazelles (except that which is announced unto you) except that which is recited to you in this surah, (game being unlawful when ye are on pilgrimage) or in the Sacred Precinct. (Lawful to you are all the beasts of cattle except that which will be announced to you,) means, except the specific circumstances that prohibit some of these which will be announced to you. " Here, Allah states, "Just as We allowed the meat of cattle in all conditions and circumstances, then do not hunt game when in the state of Ihram, for this is the decision of Allah, Who is the Most Wise in all that He commands and forbids. If on some occasions even permitted things are forbidden, as is evident from orders applicable while in the state of ihram or during sacred months, he should willingly accept this.

**He commands what He wills.**

Although this Ayah contains a command that takes effect after the end of a state of prohibition (during Ihram in this case), the Ayah, in fact, brings back the ruling that was previously in effect. If the previous ruling was an obligation, the new command will uphold that obligation, and such is the case with recommended and permissible matters. He makes lawful and prohibits what He wills whether you are in a state of ritual consecration or not. Allah decides to permit and prohibit as He wills in accordance with His wisdom. No one can compel Him or object to His decision. Towards the end of the verse, it was said: ‌ which means that Allah Almighty ordains what He wills. Verily God decrees whatever He desires in the way of making things lawful or otherwise and there can be no objection thereto.

2.text:
"O believers! Do not violate Allah's rituals ˹of pilgrimage˺" is the first command of the verse, and the rituals are the rites that mark the pilgrimage, the things set apart for Allah that no one may profane. The list that follows names them one by one so nothing in it is left unnamed: "the sacred months, the sacrificial animals, the ˹offerings decorated with˺ garlands". The sacred months are the months in which fighting is stopped and the rites stand. The sacrificial animals are the offerings brought for the House, and the garlands are hung on them so that all who see them know the animal is an offering and leave it alone. Then "nor those ˹pilgrims˺ on their way to the Sacred House seeking their Lord's bounty and pleasure" widens the protection from the rites to the people who travel to them, and the verse names what they are seeking, provision from trade and the pleasure of Allah by means of the pilgrimage, so the people heading for the House stand inside the same protection as the House itself. The hatred of a people who once barred you from the Sacred Mosque is not a way to interfere with any of it. After the protection comes its edge: "When pilgrimage has ended, you are allowed to hunt", so what is not lawful in the state of pilgrimage is lawful again once the discharge comes, and one act changes its ruling with the change of state. Then "Do not let the hatred of a people who once barred you from the Sacred Mosque provoke you to transgress" turns from the rites to the heart, and the verse is answering the wish to fight back at those who stopped the pilgrims and raided the cattle, and it makes the hatred itself the thing held back, so the wrong done by others is not met by a wrong in the sacred months or against the pilgrims. "Cooperate with one another in goodness and righteousness, and do not cooperate in sin and transgression" sets the rule for dealing with anyone, in this case or any other: help one another to what is enjoined and refuse one another help to sin and to overstepping the bounds. "And be mindful of Allah. Surely Allah is severe in punishment" closes on the one before whom all this stands, and the mindfulness is abstinence from what is evil and obedience to what He has commanded, and the warning is given in the clearest words so that no one treats the sacred months and the pilgrims as little.

**What must not be profaned from Allah's rituals.**

O you who believe do not profane God’s sacraments sha‘ā’ir is the plural of sha‘īra that is the ritual ceremonies of the religion by hunting game while you are on pilgrimage nor the sacred month by fighting in it nor the offering that is the boon offered in the Meccan Sanctuary by interfering with it nor the garlands qalā’id is the plural of qilāda and these made from the trees around the Sanctuary were placed around it the offering to protect it in other words do not interfere with these offerings or with those who place them; nor violate the sanctity of those repairing those heading to the Sacred House by fighting them who are seeking bounty provision from their Lord through commerce and His beatitude by resorting to Him as they the Meccans pagans falsely claimed this was abrogated by the barā’a verse of sūrat al-Tawba Q. 94. (O ye who believe! Profane not Allah's monuments) do not make lawful the abstention from all of Allah's rites (nor the Sacred Month) nor attacking people in the Sacred Month (nor the offerings) nor the taking of offerings which are made to the House (nor the garlands) nor the taking of the garlands which are hung by the advent of the Sacred Month, (nor those repairing to the Sacred House) nor attacking those who head for Allah's Sacred House, i.e. the pilgrims of al-Yamamah-the clan of the idolater Bakr Ibn Wa'il-and the traders of the idolater Shurayh Ibn Dabi'ah, (seeking the grace) provision (and pleasure of Allah) by means of the pilgrimage. The first relates to the sanctity of the signs, symbols or hallmarks of Allah with the specific instruction to stay away from desecrating them. O you who believe in Allah, follow His Messenger and practice His laws, do not violate the sanctity of those things that Allah has instructed you to honour.

**The sacrificial animal, the garlands and the offerings.**

Do not violate the sacrificial animal by siezing it or preventing it from reaching its place of sacrifice. (nor of the Hady brought for sacrifice, nor the garlands,) means, do not abandon the practice of bringing the Hady (sacrificial animals) to the Sacred House, as this ritual is a form of honoring the symbols of Allah. When the Muslims wanted to get him, Allah, exalted is He, revealed (O ye who believe! Profane not Allah's monuments), by monuments here is meant that which is offered for Allah, even if those who offer it profess a religion other than Islam .

**Those heading to the Sacred House seeking provision and pleasure.**

(and pleasure.) Ibn 'Abbas said that the word 'pleasure' in the Ayah refers to, "seeking Allah's pleasure by their Hajj." 'Ikrimah, As-Suddi and Ibn Jarir mentioned that this Ayah was revealed concerning Al-Hutam bin Hind Al-Bakri, who had raided the cattle belonging to the people of Al-Madīnah. It is also said that this means: they seek provision by means of trade and also Allah's pleasure. When the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace went to perform the pilgrimage in the year of Hudaybiyyah, he heard the chanting Labbayk from the pilgrims of al-Yamamah. Not violating the sanctity of such people means that they should neither be stopped during their journey nor should any pain be caused to them.

**When pilgrimage has ended, you are allowed to hunt.**

But when you are discharged from pilgrimage inviolability then hunt for game a command denoting permission. (But when you finish the Ihram, then hunt,) When you end your Ihram, it is permitted for you to hunt game, which was prohibited for you during Ihram. (But when ye have left the sacred territory) after the days of Tashriq, (then go hunting (if ye will) if you will, go hunt wild game. Stay away from those things that are prohibited when you are in the state of pilgrim sanctity, such as wearing your normal clothing, and those things that are prohibited within the Sanctuary, such as hunting.

**The hatred of a people who barred you from the Sacred Mosque.**

And let not hatred read shana’ānu or shan’ānu of a people that because they barred you from the Sacred Mosque cause you to commit aggression against them by killing them or otherwise. (And let not your hatred of a folk) the hatred of the people of Makkah (who (once) stopped your going to the Inviolable Place of Worship) on the Day of al-Hudaybiyyah (seduce you) drive you (to transgress) against the pilgrims of the clan of Bakr Ibn Wa'il; (but help ye one another unto righteousness) acts of obedience (and pious duty) shunning transgressions. The Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and his Household and give him peace, and his Companions were in Hudaybiyyah when the idolaters barred them from entering the Sacred House. But under extraordinary circumstances, he becomes a different man. For example, the occasion arises when somebody’s opposition irritates him. Why not attack them, take their animals and finish them off?

**Cooperating in goodness, and not in sin and transgression.**

Help one another to righteousness by doing that to which you were enjoined and piety by refraining from what you have been forbidden; do not help one another ta‘āwanū one of the two original tā’ letters in tata‘āwanū has been omitted to sin acts of disobedience and enmity transgression of God’s bounds. (Help not one another unto sin) contraventions (and transgression) against the pilgrims of the clan of Bakr Ibn Wa'il, (but keep your duty to Allah) fear Allah in that which He has commanded and prohibited you. Ibn Jarir said that, "Ithm means abandoning what Allah has ordained, while transgression means overstepping the limits that Allah set in your religion, along with overstepping what Allah has ordered concerning yourselves and others. About cooperating in what is righteousness and the fear of Allah, the Holy Prophet said: which means: It is the most difficult task in the present world to support those who are on the right path and ignore those who are not on the right path as they have all the wordly glories by their side. If others co-opearate with one who indulges in such oppressive activity this will amount to helping in the commission of a sin. The word, Taqwa means abstinence from what is evil.

3.text:
"Forbidden to you are carrion, blood, and swine" opens the verse with three things named in the plainest terms, and the word for carrion covers whatever dies of itself and is not slaughtered, the blood is what has been spilt and flows, and the flesh of swine is named alongside them with no exception given in the list. Then "what is slaughtered in the name of any other than Allah" moves from what the animal is to how it is killed, and the condition is the name taken over it at the time of slaughter, so meat that is pure in itself becomes unlawful when the name of an idol or a false deity is invoked over it instead of His name. The next run names the deaths that leave the animal unslaughtered: "what is killed by strangling, beating, a fall, or by being gored to death", the animal strangled with a rope, the animal beaten down, the animal fallen from a height, and the animal gored by the horns of another, and each one is an animal that died without the cut that makes meat lawful. "what is partly eaten by a predator unless you slaughter it" then gives the edge of the list, since a beast of prey that has devoured such an animal leaves it as carrion, but if you reach it while it still breathes life and slaughter it duly, it is lawful to you. "and what is sacrificed on altars" closes the list on the stones and monuments set up for other than Allah. "You are also forbidden to draw lots for decisions" turns from food to a practice, the divining arrows by which people used to decide their affairs, some marked with a command and some with a prohibition, and "This is all evil" names the whole practice as a rebellion against obedience rather than a small practice of custom. Then the verse takes in the day it was revealed and the state of those who heard it: "Today the disbelievers have given up all hope of undermining your faith", since they had despaired of the religion and now saw its strength, and the wording ends that hope in the clearest words. "So do not fear them, fear Me" turns the fear around, and the one to be mindful of is the one who perfected it. "Today I have perfected your faith for you, completed My favour upon you, and chosen Islam as your way" names the day as the day of the pilgrimage and the perfection as the rulings and obligations of the religion, so that after it nothing about what is lawful or unlawful was revealed, and the favour is completed and the way chosen. The verse then closes with the one case these rulings do not close: "But whoever is compelled by extreme hunger, not intending to sin, then surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful", so the one constrained by emptiness who consumes what has been forbidden him, without inclining purposely to sin, falls under the forgiving and the merciful named at the end, while the one who purposely inclines to it is not given that leave, and the unlawful things stay unlawful for everyone exactly as they were.

**What is forbidden of the animals, and what the allusion to the soul carries.**

Forbidden to you is carrion that is the consumption of it and blood that is what has been spilt as mentioned in sūrat al-An‘ām Q. 6145 and the flesh of swine and what has been hallowed to other than God in that it was sacrificed in the name of something other than Him and the beast strangled to death and the beast beaten down to death and the beast fallen from a height to its death and the beast gored to death by another and what beasts of prey have devoured of such animals — except for what you have sacrificed duly catching it while it still breathes life and then sacrificing it — and what has been sacrificed in the name of idols nusub is the plural of nusāb and that you apportion that is that you demand an oath or a ruling through the divining of arrows azlām the plural of zalam or zulam which is a qidh ‘a small arrow’ without feathers or a head. He has also forbidden you from spilled blood; pig’s meat; an animal on which other than the name of Allah was taken at the time of slaughter; an animal that was strangled or beaten to death, or one that fell from a high place; or an animal that was gored by another animal and an animal that was hunted by a predator, such as a lion, tiger or wolf, unless you reach any of these animals while they are alive and you slaughter them – in which case they will be lawful for you. For the same reason, in the Islamic law, the consumption of all types of dead animals is also forbidden, because the blood of a dead animal immediately gets absorbed in its flesh. (Or, flowing blood - 6:145) in another verse of the Holy Qur'an, it was made clear that blood here means blood which flows. By way of allusion He is saying that when this Adamic soul is killed by the sword of struggle in the path of discipline according to the Shariah-that is, when it has been subjugated by the religion and come to be commanded by the Shariah, made a servant and abased by the burden of obedience-the soul with this description is pure. But whenever a soul dies in the darkness of its own heedlessness such that it no longer perceives the work of the religion and exerts no effort in the limits set down by the Shariah, this soul is like the carrion whose body is defiled and nearness to which is forbidden.

**What is slaughtered in a name other than Allah.**

Whoever does not do so, mentioning other than Allah's Name, such as the name of an idol, a false deity or a monument, when slaughtering, he makes this meat unlawful, according to the consensus. Similarly, meat that is somehow polluted by polytheistic belief is forbidden; for example, the meat of an animal slaughtered by invoking any name other than that of God or the meat of animals in order to attain nearness to (or to appease) anybody other than God. If so, this too, according to a consensus of Muslim jurists, is unlawful under the injunction of ‌ (what has been invoked upon with [ a name ] other than that of Allah). (You can use what makes blood flow and you can eat what is slaughtered with the Name of Allah. But do not use teeth or claws (in slaughtering). I will tell you why, as for teeth, they are bones, and claws are used by Ethiopians for slaughtering.)" Allah said next,. He has forbidden you from those animals that were sacrificed for idols.

**The divining arrows and why it is called wickedness.**

They would use them for abitrations and when they commanded them they obeyed and if they prohibited them they would desist; that is wickedness a rebellion against obedience. He has also prohibited you from drawing lots to know whether something is destined for you or not, or to use as a means of making a decision when intending to do something or not. " My Lord commands me " , and on others " My Lord forbids me " and then use the divination method associated with it to decide their affairs, and so Allah prohibited them from engaging in such activity. Forbidden to you are carrion and blood, the flesh of swine, that which has been offered up to other than God, the strangled, the beaten down, the fallen, the gored, what has been eaten by predators-except what you slaughter-what is sacrificed on stone alters, and that which you al lot by divining arrows-that is ungodliness.

**Why the disbelievers have given up all hope.**

And on the Day of ‘Arafa in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage the following was revealed Today the disbelievers have despaired of your religion of you apostatising from it having hoped for it earlier for now they perceived its strength; therefore do not fear them but fear Me. Today the disbelievers have lost hope that you will leave the religion of Islam, because they see its strength. This is why Allah commanded His believing servants to observe patience, to be steadfast in defying and contradicting the disbelievers, and to fear none but Allah. This is because 'Din' (Faith) is demonstrated by what the members of the Community do while the consummation of 'Ni'mah' (Blessing) is directly from Al-mighty Allah (Ibn al-Qayyim, Tafsir).

**Today I have perfected your faith for you.**

Today I have perfected your religion for you that is its rulings and obligations after this verse nothing about what is lawful or unlawful was revealed and I have completed My favour upon you by perfecting it your religion but it is also said by effecting their safe entry into Makkah; and I have approved chosen Islam for you as religion. ‘Today I have perfected your religion for you’ i.e. the commandments that were to be given to you have all been given. (This day) the day of the pilgrimage (have I perfected your religion for you) I have elucidated to you the prescriptions of your religion: the lawful and the unlawful, the commands and the prohibitions (and completed My favour unto you) I have completed My blessing upon you in that, after today, no idolater will ever gather with you in 'Arafat, Mina, in the circumambulation around the Ka'bah, and in the coming and going between al-Safa and al-Marwah, (and have chosen for you as religion al-Islam. This legacy was worth the best of preservation and commemoration and this legacy was not only preserved but made mandatory for all succeeding generations as an obligatory part of their religion and faith.

**The leave given by hunger and compulsion.**

But whoever is constrained by emptiness by hunger to consume some of what has been forbidden him and consumes it not inclining purposely to sin to an act of disobedience — then God is Forgiving to him for what he has consumed Merciful to him by permitting it to him in contrast to the one who purposely inclines to sin that is the one actively engaged in it such as a waylayer or a criminal for whom such consumption is forbidden. Towards the end of the Verse, the statement: ‌ ‌ to (Allah is Most-Forgiving, Very-Merciful) makes a pointed reference to the fact that these unlawful things are still unlawful as they already were, but only such a person has been given leave because of the state of compulsion he may be in. However, God by His special grace has made the allowance that any starving person who has to choose between death and taking forbidden food may opt for the latter. Hence this carrion is worse than that carrion, and its prohibition is greater.

4.text:
"They ask you, O Prophet, what is permissible for them to eat". "Say, What is good and lawful" is where the verse starts, and the two quoted parts sit against each other on purpose: the question is put to the Prophet by people who wanted to know the rule of the hunt, men who had been commanded to kill and wanted to know what game the animals of prey make lawful for them, and the answer is given at once, before any detail, so the request and its reply stand in one line. The two words of the reply open the answer together, the good and pure things of food made lawful for you, with no condition on them beyond being good, and the plain case of food is settled before the case the question was really about. Then the answer names the case the question was really about: "Also what is caught by your hunting animals and birds of prey which you have trained as instructed by Allah", and the hunting creatures are the dogs and the wildcats and the birds that catch, trained as hounds and taught the art of hunting, taught of what Allah taught you of its methods, and the word for them in the verse also carries the animals that wound or injure their quarry. The condition is in the training itself: the beast is to be one that you have groomed to catch and bring back, not one that starts eating what it catches, and the trained creature is known by returning after it is sent out, by being curbed when cried at, and by seizing the quarry without eating of it. "So eat what they catch for you" then makes the ruling, and it stands even when the beast kills the game, as long as it has not eaten any of it, because the catch is counted for the trainer and not for the beast. "but mention the Name of Allah over it first" attaches one condition to the eating, and the mention is placed either over the immolating of the game or over the sending of the trained dogs upon it, and the verse names the mention over the act itself. "And be mindful of Allah. Surely Allah is swift in reckoning" closes as these passages close, and the mindfulness is fulfilling His instructions and staying away from His prohibitions, and the swift reckoning is severe, so the hunt made lawful is not a leave to drop the obligations of religion for the sake of chasing game.

**What is good and lawful, and what the question was.**

(They ask thee) O Muhammad; the people who so asked were Zayd Ibn Muhalhil al-Ta'i and 'Adiyy Ibn Hatim al-Ta'i, both fishermen (what is made lawful for them) of game. O Messenger of Allah, What is lawful for us of this community that we have been commanded to kill? And so Allah, exalted is He, revealed (They ask thee (O Muhammad) what is made lawful for them. Say: good things are made lawful for you. And those beasts and birds of prey) . Some Companions had asked the Holy Prophet about the rule governing hunting with the help of a trained dog and falcon. Say ‘The good delicious things are made lawful for you; and the quarry of hunting creatures dogs wildcats or birds that catch food you have taught training them as hounds mukallibīn is a circumstantial qualifier derived from kallabtu al-kalba meaning ‘I released the hound against the quarry’ teaching them tu‘allimūnahunna is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the subject of mukallibīn ‘training them as hounds’ in other words ‘disciplining them’ of what God has taught you of the art of hunting; so eat what they have caught for you even if they have killed it as long as they have not eaten any of it. All those things which are considered clean and perfectly formed in the eyes of nature, and all those animals whose nature is compatible with human nature, are all legitimate and permissible for human consumption. (while He has explained to you in detail what is forbidden to you, except under compulsion of necessity) After that, Allah said,.

**The hunting animals and birds of prey you have trained.**

Say ‘The good delicious things are made lawful for you; and the quarry of hunting creatures dogs wildcats or birds that catch food you have taught training them as hounds mukallibīn is a circumstantial qualifier derived from kallabtu al-kalba meaning ‘I released the hound against the quarry’ teaching them tu‘allimūnahunna is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the subject of mukallibīn ‘training them as hounds’ in other words ‘disciplining them’ of what God has taught you of the art of hunting; so eat what they have caught for you even if they have killed it as long as they have not eaten any of it. Allah has permitted you to eat any food that is pure and also what is hunted by trained animals that have canines, such as dogs, cheetahs, or birds that have talons such as falcons. A hint towards this condition is embedded in the word, ‌ "Al-Jawarih" (birds and beasts of prey) which also means animals which wound or injure. Hunting by a trained hunting animal is permissible because he catches the hunted animals on behalf of his master. These are animals that you train to hunt as Allah has blessed you with knowledge of its methods, such that they follow instructions and leave something when told to do so. These carnivores that are trained to catch game are called Jawarih in Arabic, a word that is derived from Jarh, meaning, what one earns.

**How the trained beast is known.**

This is in contrast to the untrained hunting creatures whose catch is not lawful for consumption the mark of these being trained hunting creatures is that they should return after they have been sent out that they can be curbed when cried at and that they can seize the quarry without eating of it; the minimum number of times by which this may be known is three. If they eat any of it then it cannot be counted as ‘what they have caught’ for their trainers and is consequently unlawful for consumption as reported in hadīth in both of the Sahīhs of Bukhārī and Muslim — therein it is also mentioned that a catch made by an arrow over which God’s name is mentioned is equivalent in lawfulness to the catch of trained hunting creatures. When the beast is trained, and it catches the game for its owner who mentioned Allah's Name when he sent the beast after the game, then this game is allowed according to the consensus of scholars, even if it was killed. The functional principle given here is that the dog should have been groomed in a manner that it should, when released at the prey, catch it and bring it back to you - not that it starts eating it.

**Mention the Name of Allah over it first.**

(Say: good things) all the immolated ones (are made lawful for you. And those beasts and birds of prey which ye have trained as hounds are trained, ye teach them) to abstain from eating game (that which Allah taught you) as Allah has taught you; (so eat of that which they) the trained dogs (catch for you and mention Allah's name upon it) upon immolating your game; and it is also said: upon sending the trained dogs upon the game, (and observe your duty to Allah) fear Allah about eating the meat of carrion. You may eat any game caught by such animals, even if they kill them, as long as you take the name of Allah when releasing them. When the beast is trained, and it catches the game for its owner who mentioned Allah's Name when he sent the beast after the game, then this game is allowed according to the consensus of scholars, even if it was killed.

**And be mindful of Allah. Surely Allah is swift in reckoning.**

Be mindful of Allah by fulfilling His instructions and staying away from His prohibitions. (Lo! Allah is swift to take account) His punishment is severe; it is also said that this means: when He is swift when He takes people to task. And those Jawarih (beasts and birds of prey) which you have trained as hounds, training and teaching them (to catch) in the manner as directed to you by Allah; so eat of what they catch for you, but pronounce the Name of Allah over it, and have Taqwa of Allah. Finally, at the end of the verse, there comes the instruction that hunting through a beast of prey has no doubt been made lawful by Al-mighty Allah, but, it is not permissible to ignore Salah and other necessary religious obligations for the sake of having fun chasing game.

5.text:
"Today all good, pure foods have been made lawful for you". "Similarly, the food of the People of the Book is permissible for you and yours is permissible for them" opens the verse on the day it was brought down, the day of the pilgrimage when the verse and those before it were revealed, and the opening settles food in one line before anything else is touched. The good are the wholesome things, and the lawful here carries no condition beyond being good, so what is pure in itself is open. The second sentence then takes the case of others: the food of the People of the Book means the animals they have properly slaughtered, and the verse makes it lawful in both directions, theirs for you and yours for them, so a Muslim may eat of what a Jew or a Christian slaughters and they may eat of what a Muslim slaughters, and the word for food here is the word for the slaughtered animal. Then "And ˹permissible for you in marriage˺ are chaste believing women as well as chaste women of those given the Scripture before you" turns from food to marriage, and it names the two groups in the same line, the free chaste women of the believers and the free chaste women of those who received the Scripture before you, and the word chaste is what the ruling stands on, since the verse is talking about women who do not commit fornication. The condition comes in the next phrase: "as long as you pay them their dowries in wedlock", so the marriage is tied to the dowry given to them in marriage and lived with in honour, and the payment is what separates the marriage from everything else. "neither fornicating nor taking them as mistresses" then names what is refused on both sides of it, the open fornication and the secret taking of lovers, and the wording was brought down about the women of Makkah when they boasted to the women of Madīnah, so the two are named to close the doors around the permission. The verse ends on the limit of all these permissions: "And whoever rejects the faith, all their good deeds will be void ˹in this life˺ and in the Hereafter they will be among the losers", so the one who denies the faith has his prior good work fail and count for nothing, and without faith good deeds have no reality or value, and the condition for good actions to be accepted is true faith, and in the Hereafter he is among the losers, deprived of what the people of faith are given. The next verse takes up the heart of that faith in the prayer.

**The day of Arafah and the good things made lawful.**

Here, 'this day' means the day on which this verse and those before it have been revealed, that is, the Day of Arafah in the Last Hajj of Hijrah 10. (This day) the day of the pilgrimage (are good things) that which has been immolated (made lawful for you. The food) the animals immolated (of those who have received the Scripture is lawful for you) as long as it is not prohibited, (and your food) your immolated animals (is lawful for them) both the Jews and Christians can consume that which the Muslims immolate. Today the good the delicious things are permitted to you and the food of those who were given the Scripture that is animals slaughtered by the Jews and Christians is permitted to you and permitted to them is your food. Here, the command to be righteous in deeds refers itself back to the command to eat from what is Halal (lawful) because without eating Halal, righteous deeds cannot be imagined. And let us keep in mind that unlawful income from theft, robbery, bribery, interest, gambling and evils like that, once it becomes part of anyone's body, will inevitably remove one farther from humanity and nearer to 'satanic nature.' Hence, says the Holy Qur'an: ‌ (O' Messengers, eat from good things [ made lawful as sustenance ] and do righteous deeds - 23:51). However elaborate the Law relating to forbidden and permissible things is made, it is finally man’s intention which debars him from certain things and leads him towards certain others. (and your food is lawful to them.) means, you are allowed to feed them from your slaughtered animals.

**The food of the People of the Book.**

Therefore, in the present verse, it is a consensus of the Ummah that the 'food of the People of the Book' means their properly slaughtered animal. According to the consensus of Sahabah and Tabi in (the Companions and their Successors), the word 'Ta am' (food) at this place means 'properly slaughtered animals' (Dhabihah). Today Allah has allowed you to eat those things that are wholesome, and the animals slaughtered by the Jews and Christians who are the People of the Scripture. Therefore, this part of the Ayah is not to inform the People of the Scriptures that they are allowed to eat our food – unless we consider it information for us about the ruling that they have – i. e, that they are allowed all types of foods over which Allah's Name was mentioned, whether slaughtered according to their religion or otherwise. It is recorded in the Sahih that 'Abdullah bin Mughaffal said, "While we were attacking the fort of Khaybar, a person threw a leather bag containing fat, and I ran to take it and said, 'I will not give anyone anything from this container today.' But when I turned I saw the Prophet (standing behind) while smiling.

**The chaste women made lawful in marriage.**

Likewise the believing free married women and the married women of those who were given the Scripture before you are permitted to you for marriage if you give them their wages their dowries in wedlock in marriage and not illicitly fornicating overtly with them or taking them as lovers so as to fornicate with them secretly. He has permitted you to marry free, chaste women from the believers, as well as free, chaste women from the Jews and Christians who received scripture before you. But Muslim males have been permitted, subject to certain special conditions to marry women belonging to communities, who are in possession of the Holy scriptures. It may be expected of her that once she enters marital life, she may be influenced by her Muslim husband and Muslim society, and thus her marriage may become a starting point for her entry into Islam. This Ayah is talking about women who do not commit fornication, as evident by the word 'chaste'.

**Their dowries in wedlock, and neither fornicating nor taking them as mistresses.**

Likewise the believing free married women and the married women of those who were given the Scripture before you are permitted to you for marriage if you give them their wages their dowries in wedlock in marriage and not illicitly fornicating overtly with them or taking them as lovers so as to fornicate with them secretly. This is if you give them their dowries and you are trying to stay away from committing an immoral action, such as adultery or fornication, by taking them as lovers. (And so are the) free (virtuous women of the believers) are lawful for you to marry (and the virtuous women of those who received the Scripture before you) lawful for you to marry (when ye give them their marriage portions) their dowry, in surplus of the price given to the prostitute in exchange for sex (and live with them in honour) in wedlock, (not in) flagrant (fornication, nor taking them as secret concubines.) This was revealed about the women of Makkah when they boasted to the women of Medina.

**Whoever rejects the faith, and deeds that come to nothing.**

Whoever disbelieves in faith that is whose apostatises his prior good work has indeed failed and so it counts for nothing and he will not be rewarded for it and in the Hereafter he shall be among the losers if he dies in this state of unbelief. ‘The deeds of anyone who rejects the faith will come to nothing’ i.e. without Faith, good deeds have no reality or value. Yet whosoever disbelieves in Allah and His laws which He has given to his slaves, then his actions are void, because the condition for good actions to be accepted is true faith. (Whoso denieth the faith) Allah's divine Oneness, (his work is vain) in this world (and he will be among the losers in the Hereafter) he will be of those who have been duped since he will be deprived of Paradise and enter hell.

6.text:
"O believers! When you rise up for prayer" sets the occasion of everything that follows, and the address is to people already in faith being taught the state they must stand in, and the wording covers the moment a person intends to go to pray. Then the acts come in order: "wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows, wipe your heads, and wash your feet to the ankles", and the order itself carries a rule, since the wiping of the head is placed between the washing of the hands and the washing of the feet to show that a specific order is required during the purification of these limbs. The washing takes in the elbows and the ankles, as they are clarified in the Sunna, and the wiping of the head is with the hand adhering closely to it without excessive water pouring over, and the minimum required to fulfil the stipulation is acceptable, which is the wiping of some of the hair. The verse then names the two states this washing stands for: "And if you are in a state of ˹full˺ impurity, then take a full bath", so the major state is met by the full bath with water, and the minor state by the washing already described, and in normal circumstances the washing is enough to create feelings of cleanliness in a person, while the state that follows intimacy is an extraordinary condition. The case of no water comes next: "But if you are ill, on a journey, or have relieved yourselves, or have been intimate with your wives and cannot find water", and each case is named as it came down about a man who was sick and could not use water, and the illness is the one made worse by water or the healing delayed by it, and the journey is travelling, and the relieved yourselves stands for the privy, and the touching of women is what is already known, and all of it hangs on one condition, that you have made the effort to look for water and cannot find it. Then "then purify yourselves with clean earth by wiping your faces and hands" gives the substitute, the clean earth struck with the hands and wiped over the faces and the hands, and the wiping is to encompass the whole of these two parts, and it is a mercy and an opening for the sick and the traveller rather than a difficulty. "It is not Allah's Will to burden you, but to purify you and complete His favour upon you, so perhaps you will be grateful" closes on the reason behind the whole passage: no constraint is imposed in the obligations of washing and purification with dust, and the purpose is the purification from filth and sins and the perfection of the grace given through Islam by explaining the laws of the religion, so that the one washed gives thanks for His graces.

**The washing of the faces, hands and feet, and the wiping of the head.**

O you who believe when you stand up that is when you intend to go to pray and you are in a state of ritual impurity wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows that is including them the elbows as is clarified in the Sunna; and wipe your heads the bā’ in bi-ru’ūsikum is for ‘adherence’ that is to say wipe over the head adhering the hand closely without excessive water pouring over; the noun ra’s ‘head’ is generic and so the minimum required to fulfil the stipulation is acceptable which is the wiping of some of the hair as al-Shāfi‘ī asserts; and your feet read wa-arjulakum in the accusative as a supplement to aydīyakum; or wa-arjulikum in the genitive because of its adjacency to the genitive bi-ru’ūsikum up to the ankles that is including them the ankles as is clarified in the Sunna and they are the two protruding bones at the juncture of the legs and the feet. (wash your face, and your hands up to the elbows, and lightly rub your heads) as you please (and (wash) your feet) above the sole of the feet (up to the ankles. And if ye are unclean) if you are in a state of major ritual impurity, (purify yourselves) with water. O you who believe in Allah, follow His Messenger and practice His laws, when you intend to stand up to offer the prayer and you are in the state of minor ritual impurity, then perform ablution by washing your faces and then your hands together with the elbows, then wiping your heads and finally washing your feet together with the ankles. ’ When he washes his feet, this action of his becomes the entreaty before his Lord, that He may cleanse his feet of the dust of evil and make them (his feet) never tread any path except the path of righteousness and justice.

**The wiping of the head between the hands and the feet.**

The interposing of the wiping of the head between the mention of the hands and the feet which are washed is intended to show the requirement of a specific order during the purification of these limbs as al-Shāfi‘ī asserts. ’ Thereafter, when he takes water in his hands and massages his head with his hands, his whole existence is moulded by the prayers, ‘O, God! Initiating the process of ablution (wudu) when a man puts water on his hands, he is, in effect, praying, ‘O, God!

**The full bath for the state of impurity.**

’ In normal circumstances, ablution is enough to create feelings of cleanliness in man, but the state of impurity (resulting from sex) is an extraordinary condition. If you are sick and you fear that the sickness will get worse or the healing will be delayed, or if you are on a journey even though you are not sick, or if you are in the state of minor ritual impurity, such as after going to the toilet, or in a state of major ritual impurity, such as after having had sexual intercourse, and you do not find water to purify yourselves with, despite having searched for it, then make use of the ground by striking it with your hands and then wiping over your faces and then wiping your hands with it.

**When water cannot be found: the clean earth.**

If you are defiled purify wash yourselves; but if you are sick with an illness made worse by water or on a journey travelling or if any of you comes from the privy that is if he has defecated or you have touched women as mentioned already in the verse in sūrat al-Nisā’ Q. 443 and you cannot find water having made the effort to look for it then head for seek wholesome dust that is clean earth and wipe your faces and your hands including the elbows with it using two strikes the bā’ of bi-wujūhikum ‘your faces’ denotes ‘adherence’; it is explained in the Sunna that the requirement here is for the wiping to encompass the whole of these two parts. This is why He allowed you to use Tayammum when you are ill and when you do not find water, to make things comfortable for you and as mercy for you. If you find no water, have recourse to goodly dust. This was revealed about 'Abdullah Ibn 'Awf (or on a journey, or one of you cometh from the closet) or one of you has urinated or defecated, (or ye have had (sexual) contact with women) or had sex with women, (and ye find not water) you are unable to use water, (then go to clean, high ground and rub your faces) with the first blow (and your hands) with the second blow (with some of it) i.e. some of the dust.

**It is not Allah's Will to burden you.**

(Allah would not place a burden) constraint (on you, but He would purify you) by means of dry ablution from minor and major ritual impurities (and would perfect His grace) His favour (upon you, that ye may give thanks) for His blessing and legal dispensation. Allah does not wish to make the laws difficult for you by forcing you to use water that may lead to harm or difficulty. God does not desire to make any hardship for you any constraint in the obligations He has imposed on you with regard to ablution washing and purification with dust; but He desires to purify you of filth and sins and that He may perfect His grace upon you through Islam by explaining the laws of the religion; so that you might give thanks for His graces.

**But to purify you and complete His favour upon you.**

(Allah would not place a burden) constraint (on you, but He would purify you) by means of dry ablution from minor and major ritual impurities (and would perfect His grace) His favour (upon you, that ye may give thanks) for His blessing and legal dispensation. (Purity is half of faith and Al-Hamdu Lillah (all the thanks are due to Allah) fills the Mizan (the Scale). And Subhan Allah and Allahu Akbar (all praise is due to Allah, and Allah is the Most Great) fills what is between the heaven and earth. As-Sawm (the fast) is a Junnah (a shield), Sabr (patience) is a light, Sadaqah (charity) is evidence (of faith) and the Qur'an is proof for, or against you. Every person goes out in the morning and ends up selling himself, he either frees his soul or destroys it.) When this purity is gained, the servant is adorned with obedience and reverence. God does not desire to make any hardship for you any constraint in the obligations He has imposed on you with regard to ablution washing and purification with dust; but He desires to purify you of filth and sins and that He may perfect His grace upon you through Islam by explaining the laws of the religion; so that you might give thanks for His graces.

7.text:
"Remember Allah's favour upon you and the covenant He made with you when you said, "We hear and obey"" opens on two things at once, the gift already given and the promise already made, and the remembering is put first so the promise is not taken as one more duty laid on the one who has already been favoured. The favour is the grace that came through Islam and the hands that were held back from you, since the verse answers a state in which some people had planned to stretch out their hands against the believers and Allah held back their hands, and the favour named here is the safety given before the covenant was taken. The covenant is the pledge with which He bound you, the promise taken when they embraced Islam and said to the Messenger of Allah to hear and obey, in times when they are active and otherwise, even if they were passed on for rights, and not to dispute leadership with its rightful people, and the wording of the vow is plain: we give our pledge of obedience to hear and to follow in ease or difficulty. The saying is put in the verse in its shortest form, "We hear and obey", so that the hearing and the obeying stand together with nothing between them, and the words are the words of a vow that binds God and His subject, and the subject vows that he will remain God-fearing in his life in this world, and God guarantees that He will be his guardian in this world and in the Hereafter. The verse then puts the whole weight of the covenant into one command: "And be mindful of Allah", and the mindfulness is fulfilling His instructions including His promises and avoiding His prohibitions, so keeping the covenant is the shape of all duty toward God, and the one who has given this pledge has to prove his fulfillment of it. "Surely Allah knows best what is ˹hidden˺ in the heart" closes where the covenant began, since the pledge was taken from the heart before it was said, and the knowledge named here is of the secrets and thoughts the hearts conceal, of loyalty and betrayal, and nothing is hidden from Him, so the one who keeps the vow and the one who breaks it are not alike before Him.

**The favour that is remembered first.**

(Remember Allah's grace) recollect Allah's blessing (upon you) through faith (and His covenant) pledge (by which He bound you) with which He commanded you on the Day of the Covenant (when you said: We hear) Your words, O our Lord, (and we obey) Your command; (and keep your duty to Allah) fear Allah in that which He commanded and prohibited you. Remember Allah’s favour upon you by guiding you to Islam and the promise He took from you when you said at the time of pledging allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ to listen and follow in ease or difficulty: Remember the favor of Allah unto you when some people desired (made a plan) to stretch out their hands against you, but (Allah) held back their hands from you.

**The covenant, the pledge, and the words of the vow.**

And remember God’s grace upon you through Islam and His covenant His pledge which He made He bound with you when you said to the Prophet s upon pledging allegiance to him ‘We hear and we obey’ all that you command and forbid of what we love and what we despise. This is the pledge that they used to give to the Messenger of Allah when they embraced Islam. They used to say, "We gave our pledge of obedience to the Messenger of Allah to hear and obey, in times when we are active and otherwise, even if we were passed on for rights, and not to dispute leadership with its rightful people. (Remember Allah's grace) recollect Allah's blessing (upon you) through faith (and His covenant) pledge (by which He bound you) with which He commanded you on the Day of the Covenant (when you said: We hear) Your words, O our Lord, (and we obey) Your command; (and keep your duty to Allah) fear Allah in that which He commanded and prohibited you. Faith is the vow which binds God and His subject. The subject vows that he will remain God-fearing in his life in this world, and God guarantees that He will be His subject’s guardian in this world and in the Hereafter. God’s subject has to prove his fulfillment of his vow in two ways. ‘We hear your words and we follow your instruction’.

**The hands that were stretched out and held back.**

Remember the favor of Allah unto you when some people desired (made a plan) to stretch out their hands against you, but (Allah) held back their hands from you. (Remember the favor of Allah unto you when some people desired (made a plan) to stretch out their hands against you...) (O you who believe! Remember the favor of Allah unto you when some people desired (made a plan) to stretch out their hands against you, but (Allah) withheld their hands from you.)

**The stone that was planned over the Messenger.**

Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar, Mujahid and 'Ikrimah said that this Ayah was revealed about Bani An-Nadir, who plotted to drop a stone on the head of the Messenger when he came to them for help to pay the blood money of two persons whom Muslims killed. The Jews left the execution of this plot to 'Amr bin Jihash bin Ka'b and ordered him to throw a stone on the Prophet from above, when he came to them and sat under the wall. It was also said that this Ayah reminds the Jews of the pledges and promises Allah took from them to follow Muhammad and adhere to his Law, as 'Ali bin Abi Talhah reported that Ibn 'Abbas stated.

**And be mindful of Allah, who knows what is in the hearts.**

Be mindful of Allah by fulfilling His instructions, including His promises, and avoiding His prohibitions. Surely God knows what is in the breasts that is what is in the hearts of people all the more reason for Him to have knowledge of other things. Allah says that He knows the secrets and thoughts that the hearts conceal,. (Allah knoweth what is in the breasts (of men) of loyalty and betrayal. (and have Taqwa of Allah. Verily, Allah is Well-Acquainted with what you do.) and consequently, He will reward or punish you according to your actions, whether good or evil.

8.text:
"O believers! Stand firm for Allah and bear true testimony" takes the covenant of the verse before and puts it out in the open, and the standing is upright before God in fulfilling what is His due, and the testimony is the witness given in equity and in justice, not for oppression. The witness is for Allah and not for a party, so no one is to avoid recording true evidence and stating what is the truth in honesty with Allah, so that the decision makers face no difficulty in arriving at the true, sound and just decision, and the case is not made harder for the one who comes forward with what he knows. Then "Do not let the hatred of a people lead you to injustice. Be just! That is closer to righteousness" names the danger that faces the witness and the judge alike, since the hatred of a people who wronged you is the thing that draws the testimony and the deciding of cases away from the truth, and the verse answers the malice against a people that bids a person to not doing justice, and it makes the rule stand for friend and foe alike: justice is a requirement with a friend as well as with an enemy, so be just with both. The word is put first on purpose, and the message is that a concession which is contrary to justice cannot be for Allah, and justice here is the treatment a person actually deserves, no more and no less, and observing it is nearer to the God-fearingness the verse names, and one who stands for justice stands for none but Allah. The one bound by the covenant is bound to this even when grievances and bitter memories are apt to divert him from the path of justice, and his dealings with his fellow-beings are to be based on justice and fair play, so the hatred is answered by the justice rather than by the like of it. "And be mindful of Allah. Surely Allah is All-Aware of what you do" closes the verse as the covenant closed, and the mindfulness is fulfilling His instructions and avoiding His prohibitions, and the awareness is of the justice and the injustice in every case, and He will reward or punish for the actions, whether good or evil, so nothing done in the deciding of cases or in the giving of witness is small before Him.

**Standing firm for Allah, and the witness in justice.**

(O ye who believe! Be steadfast witnesses for Allah in equity) in justice, (and let not hatred of any people) the hatred of Shurayh Ibn Shurahbil (seduce you) drive you (that ye deal not justly) with the pilgrims of the clan of Bakr Ibn Wa'il. Be witnesses for justice and not for oppression. O you who believe be upright before God in fulfilling what is His due witnesses in equity in justice. The second instruction given in these two verses is that no one should avoid recording true evidence and stating what is the truth in honesty with Allah, so that the decision makers face no difficulty in arriving at the true, sound and just decision. It is recorded in the Two Sahihs that An-Nu'man bin Bashir said, "My father gave me a gift, but 'Amrah bint Rawahah, my mother, said that she would not agree to it unless he made Allah's Messenger as a witness to it. But, what is happening here is that the first investigation of a case is handled by the police and it is, by itself, enough to drive a witness crazy by his repeated appearances at the station. O you who believe in Allah and His Messenger and follow His laws, uphold Allah’s rights over you, seeking His pleasure.

**The hatred of a people must not lead you to injustice.**

Let not hatred of a people namely the disbelievers cause you not to be just and to harm them on account of their enmity; be just towards both friend and foe that justice is nearer to God-fearing. The hatred for a people should not make you leave justice: justice is a requirement with a friend, as well as with an enemy, so be just with both. Remember the favor of Allah unto you when some people desired (made a plan) to stretch out their hands against you, but (Allah) held back their hands from you. (O you who believe! Remember the favor of Allah unto you when some people desired (made a plan) to stretch out their hands against you, but (Allah) withheld their hands from you.) Therefore, the words which follow this sentence in Surah Al-Nisa' ‌ that is, 'even though against yourselves or the parents, and the kinsfolk ...' After the sentence of Surah al-Ma'idah cited above, the words which follow in this verse are: ‌ that is, And malice against a people should not bid you to not doing justice ...' So, the essential message of this verse of Surah al-Nisa' is:

**Justice is closer to righteousness.**

Justice is closer to the fear of Allah, and oppression is closer to disrespect against Him. Justice means meting out to a person that treatment which he actually deserves—no more and no less. Although Allah said that observing justice is 'nearer to Taqwa', there is not any other course of action to take, therefore 'nearer' here means 'is'. Therefore, by bringing in the word, 'al-qist' (justice) first at that point, the message given was that the concession which is contrary to justice cannot be for Allah. (Deal justly) with them, (that is nearer to your duty) justice is nearer to God-fearingness as far as the God-fearing are concerned.

**Justice with friend and enemy, even after grievances.**

Let not hatred of a people namely the disbelievers cause you not to be just and to harm them on account of their enmity; be just towards both friend and foe that justice is nearer to God-fearing. The hatred for a people should not make you leave justice: justice is a requirement with a friend, as well as with an enemy, so be just with both. He should be bound by this principle to the extent that he should adhere to justice even when dealing with his enemies; even when grievances and bitter memories are apt to divert him from the path of justice. The second condition for the fulfillment of the vow of God’s subject is that his dealings with his fellow-beings should be based on justice and fair play.

**And be mindful of Allah. Surely Allah is All-Aware of what you do.**

Be mindful of Allah by fulfilling His instructions and avoiding His prohibitions. And fear God; surely God is aware of what you do and will requite you for it. (Observe your duty to Allah) fear Allah regarding justice and injustice. (Lo! Allah is Informed of what ye do) whether it is justice or injustice. (and have Taqwa of Allah. Verily, Allah is Well-Acquainted with what you do.) and consequently, He will reward or punish you according to your actions, whether good or evil. The subject vows that he will remain God-fearing in his life in this world, and God guarantees that He will be His subject’s guardian in this world and in the Hereafter.

9.text:
A promise stands here after the verse on justice, and it is made in the plainest terms: "Allah has promised those who believe and do good ˹His˺ forgiveness and a great reward". The promise is to those who believe and do good, and the two are named together so that neither one alone carries it, and the good are the acts of obedience regarding that which is between a person and his Lord, the deeds of righteousness that follow the faith. What is promised is then named in two words, forgiveness and a great reward, and the forgiveness is of the sins in this world, and the reward is the great wage that is Paradise, and the wording puts the forgiveness first so the one who has done wrong is not left out of the promise. The verse after it names the opposite case, so the two stand against each other, and the one who accepts the arguments of God when they are put before a man is the one who believes and does good, while the one who indulges in verbal pyrotechnics instead of accepting them is the one who denies the signs, and those who accept the argument will be held deserving of God's reward. A person who stands for justice will stand for none but Allah, and one who stands for none but Allah will do nothing but justice, so the promise here is tied to the standing that the verse before it commanded.

**What the promise is, and whom it is for.**

God has promised those who believe and perform righteous deeds an excellent promise they shall have forgiveness and a great wage that is Paradise. Verily, Allah is Well-Acquainted with what you do Allah has promised those who believe and do deeds of righteousness, that for them there is forgiveness and a great reward (i.e. Paradise)And they who disbelieve and deny Our Ayat are those who will be the dwellers of the Hell-fire O you who believe! (Allah hath promised those who believe) in Muhammad and the Qur'an (and do good works) and do acts of obedience regarding that which is between them and their Lord: Allah has made a promise to those who have faith in Allah and His messengers of forgiveness for their sins and a great reward which is to enter into Paradise.

**Believing and doing good, and what the good deeds are.**

It means that anyone who makes a good, true and justified recommendation, then, he too will get a share from the good deed of the per-son he has recommended. (Allah hath promised those who believe) in Muhammad and the Qur'an (and do good works) and do acts of obedience regarding that which is between them and their Lord: God has promised those who believe and perform righteous deeds an excellent promise they shall have forgiveness and a great wage that is Paradise.

**Forgiveness and the great reward.**

(Theirs will be forgiveness) of their sins in this world (and immense reward) in Paradise. And those who accept the argument will be held deserving of God’s reward. Allah has made a promise to those who have faith in Allah and His messengers of forgiveness for their sins and a great reward which is to enter into Paradise. God has promised those who believe and perform righteous deeds an excellent promise they shall have forgiveness and a great wage that is Paradise.

**Standing for none but Allah, and the arguments one accepts.**

It is obvious that a person who stands for justice will stand for none but Allah, and one who stands for none but Allah will do nothing but justice. (O you who believe! Stand out firmly for Allah...) meaning, in truth for the sake of Allah, not for the sake of people or for fame,. In the world, God makes His appearance felt through symbols, i.e. in the shape of such arguments as cannot be contradicted by man. When an argument of God appears before a man and he indulges in verbal pyrotechnics instead of accepting it, then this amounts to denying the signs of God.

10.text:
The verse that promised forgiveness and a great reward now names the case that stands against it: "As for those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, they are the residents of the Hellfire". The two things named in the first half are not the same: the disbelief is the state that turns away, and the denial is what a person does with the signs when they are put before him, since in the world God makes His appearance felt through symbols and arguments that cannot be contradicted, and when an argument of God appears before a man and he indulges in verbal pyrotechnics instead of accepting it, this amounts to denying the signs of God. The signs are the revelations given to the Messenger, the Qur'an itself, so the denial named here is of the words themselves. Then "they are the residents of the Hellfire" names the end of them, and the residents are the dwellers of the Fire, and they will remain in it eternally, just as a companion remains with his companion, and the punishment is for the disbelief and the rejection together. **Those who disbelieve and deny Our signs.**

And they who disbelieve and deny Our signs — they shall be the inhabitants of Hell-fire. (And they who disbelieve) in Allah (and deny Our revelations) Muhammad and the Qur'an, (such are rightful owners of hell) the dwellers of the Fire. When an argument of God appears before a man and he indulges in verbal pyrotechnics instead of accepting it, then this amounts to denying the signs of God. 11.text:
"O believers! Remember Allah's favour upon you" opens the passage on the same word the covenant passage closed with, and the remembering here is specific rather than general: "when a people sought to harm you, but He held their hands back from you". The favour is the safety given when a man came to the Messenger with the sword and was restrained from what he intended, and what the people purposed was to extend their hands against the believers to attack them, and what came of it was that He restrained their hands and turned the harm away from those they meant to reach. The wording puts the two halves against each other, the seeking to harm and the holding back, so the favour is read as the harm that was turned away, and the one who remembers it knows whom the safety came from and what was in the hearts of those who planned it. The hostilities stand here only to be answered by the justice the verse before this one commanded, since hostility against an enemy should not affect the sense of justice to the limit that a person starts working against its demands to harm his enemy. "Be mindful of Allah" then carries the same command the covenant carried, and the mindfulness is fulfilling His instructions and avoiding His prohibitions, and the favour is not remembered rightly unless it ends in the duty, and the duty here is the whole of what a person owes to the one who held the hands back. "And in Allah let the believers put their trust" closes on the posture that follows from all of it, and the trust is the reliance on Allah alone in order to achieve the religious and worldly interests, and the believers should rely on Allah rather than on the hands that were held back or on their own strength, and the next verse goes back to the first covenant of all, the one taken from the Children of Israel by their prophet that they would lead a godly life, so the trust named here is the trust of a people who have already been carried through a harm they could not turn away themselves, and the favour is remembered so that the duty and the trust after it are held up on the right ground.

**The favour remembered: the hands held back from you.**

Muhammad and his Companions (Remember Allah's favour unto you) recollect Allah's grace by driving away from you the harm of the enemy, (how a people) the people of the Banu Qurayzah (were minded to stretch out their hands against you) to kill you (but He withheld) He prevented (their hands from you) from killing you; (and keep your duty to Allah) fear Allah in relation to that which He has commanded you. O you who believe remember God’s favour upon you when a people namely Quraysh purposed to extend their hands against you in order to attack you but He restrained their hands from you and protected you from what they intended to do to you; and fear God; and in God let the believers put their trust. O you who believe in Allah and follow His Messenger, remember, with your hearts and tongues, the favours Allah has given you, such as safety and the placing of fear in the hearts of your enemies, when they intended to stretch their hands towards you in order to attack you.

**What the people intended, and what was turned away.**

O you who believe remember God’s favour upon you when a people namely Quraysh purposed to extend their hands against you in order to attack you but He restrained their hands from you and protected you from what they intended to do to you; and fear God; and in God let the believers put their trust. Muhammad and his Companions (Remember Allah's favour unto you) recollect Allah's grace by driving away from you the harm of the enemy, (how a people) the people of the Banu Qurayzah (were minded to stretch out their hands against you) to kill you (but He withheld) He prevented (their hands from you) from killing you; (and keep your duty to Allah) fear Allah in relation to that which He has commanded you. The essence of this verse from Surah al-Ma'idah is that hostility against an enemy should not affect your sense of justice to the limit that you start working against the demands of justice to harm your enemy. The Jews left the execution of this plot to 'Amr bin Jihash bin Ka'b and ordered him to throw a stone on the Prophet from above, when he came to them and sat under the wall. But when the communities blessed with Divine Scriptures go astray, they turn to the right or left of this highway.

**The sword and the man who came with it.**

This man then proceeded to the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, and found him sitting with his sword in his lap. The man took the sword out of its scabbard, moved it about but whenever he was on the point of striking the Prophet with it, Allah, glorious and majestic is He, restrained him. The man put the sword back in its scabbard and gave it back to the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, upon which Allah, exalted is He, revealed (Remember Allah's favour unto you, how a people were minded to stretch out their hands against you). A Bedouin came along, got hold of the sword belonging to the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, turned to him and said:

**Be mindful of Allah, and in Him let the believers put their trust.**

Be mindful of Allah by fulfilling His instructions and avoiding His prohibitions. Let the believers place their reliance in Allah alone, in order to achieve their religious and worldly interests. O you who believe remember God’s favour upon you when a people namely Quraysh purposed to extend their hands against you in order to attack you but He restrained their hands from you and protected you from what they intended to do to you; and fear God; and in God let the believers put their trust.

12.text:
"Allah made a covenant with the Children of Israel and appointed twelve leaders from among them and ˹then˺ said" goes back to the first covenant of all, and the verse names both halves of it, the promise taken and the men appointed to keep it, and the acknowledgement in the Torah was that they shall worship none except Allah and shall not ascribe partners to Him. The twelve leaders were raised from among them, one from each tribe to be responsible for his people's fulfilment of the covenant as a way of binding them to it, and they are called messengers in one reading and kings in another, a king to each tribe. Then comes the word behind all of it: "I am truly with you", and the help and support named here is the help promised on the condition that follows, not a bare presence, and the real cause of the Divine support and protection is the quality of the fear of Allah and the trust in Him. The condition is then given in a line of five things: "If you establish prayer, pay alms-tax, believe in My messengers, support them, and lend to Allah a good loan", and the five are the pledge itself, to lead a godly life through the prayer which has been made obligatory, to discharge the rights of others in the shape of the obligatory giving from the wealth, to acknowledge and accept the messengers sent, to assist them with the sword against the enemy and align on the side of God by supporting His prophets, and to spend the assets in the struggle for the religion of God, and the loan is the spending genuinely from the heart, given to Allah and not to a person. "I will certainly forgive your sins and admit you into Gardens under which rivers flow" names what the five earn, and the forgiveness is of the sins other than the enormities, and the Gardens are the ones beneath which rivers of water, milk, wine and honey flow, and it was only after undertaking all this and establishing a collective system for ensuring the continued fulfilment of these duties that they were entitled to the company and support named in the first half of the verse. The verse then draws the line: "And whoever among you disbelieves afterwards has truly strayed from the Right Way", so whoever of you disbelieves after that covenant has erred from the road of guidance, and the stray is from the middle way that leads to the Gardens just promised, and the ones who broke it are named in the verses after this one, so the road is plain on both sides, the covenant and its terms on one side and the stray after it on the other.

**The covenant with the Children of Israel and the twelve leaders.**

God had made a covenant with the Children of Israel for what will be mentioned shortly and We raised up there is a shift of address away from the third to the first person from among them twelve leaders from each tribe one leader to be responsible for his people’s fulfilment of the covenant as a way of binding them to it. Allah had taken a firm promise from the Children of Israel, when He appointed over them twelve chiefs who were placed in authority over them. (Allah made a covenant of old with the Children of Israel) the acknowledgement of the Children of Israel in the Torah of Muhammad, that they shall worship none except Allah and that they shall not ascribe partners to Him (and We raised among them twelve chieftains) 12 messengers; and it is said: 12 kings, a king to each tribe: A pledge was taken from the Children of Israel by their prophet that they would lead a godly life, and twelve chiefs from their twelve tribes were appointed to keep a watch over them. It is said in the verse that Almighty Allah had taken a pledge from the Bani Isra'il (The Children of Israel).

I am with you- with my help and support if you establish the prayer in the complete manner, give Zakat from your wealth, accept all of my messengers without distinction, honour them, assist them and spend in good causes. (If you establish worship) if you establish the prayer which has been made obligatory upon you (and pay the poor-due) from your wealth, (and believe in) acknowledge and accept (My messengers) who are sent to you (and support them) and assist them with the sword against the enemy, (and lend unto Allah a kindly loan) genuinely from your heart, (surely I shall remit your sins) other than the enormities, (and surely I shall bring you into Gardens beneath which) beneath its trees and habitations (rivers) rivers of water, milk, wine and honey (flow.
