Surely if la-in the lām is for oaths you establish the prayer and pay the alms and believe in My messengers and succour them help them and lend to God a goodly loan by expending in His way I will absolve you of your evil deeds and I will admit you to gardens underneath which rivers flow. If you do all of this, I will wipe out the sins you commit and I will enter you, on the Day of Judgement, into gardens with palaces overlooking flowing streams. It was only after undertaking all this and after establishing a collective system among themselves for ensuring the continued fulfillment of these duties that they were entitled to God’s company and support, and entitled to enter the aesthetic atmosphere of paradise, after being purified. It means if they fulfilled the pledge themselves and re-solved to make others do the same, Divine support shall be with them.

So whoever of you disbelieves after that covenant surely he has strayed from the right way’ he has erred from the path to Paradise al-sawā’ originally means ‘the middle way’. It is said in the verse that Almighty Allah had taken a pledge from the Bani Isra'il (The Children of Israel). Whoever disbelieves after making this promise has knowingly and deliberately deviated from the path of truth. Nonetheless, they disbelieved except five of them. They changed the words from their (right) places and have abandoned a good part of the Message that was sent to them.

13.text:
"But for breaking their covenant We condemned them and hardened their hearts" names what the breaking of the covenant earned, and the condemnation is the removal from the mercy and its effects, and the hearts were made hard against any penetration of truth, so that no good could enter them and no advice could be of benefit to them. The hardening is not left as a description only: it becomes the state in which "They distorted the words of the Scripture and neglected a portion of what they had been commanded to uphold", and the distorting is the changing of the words from their right places, the traits and the description of Muhammad in the Torah and the legal rulings exposited there, altered in words or in meanings or in recitation, and replaced with other words and given the interpretation their desires wanted, and the neglecting is the leaving of a part of what they were admonished with, the part of the Message sent to them that they abandoned. The next phrase turns to the Prophet himself: "You ˹O Prophet,˺ will always find deceit on their part, except for a few", so the treachery and the contravention are what he will ceaselessly discover from them, with the exception of the few of them who fulfil the promise taken from them, and the few are named in the readings as those who submitted themselves to Islam. Then comes the command that answers all of it: "But pardon them and bear with them. Indeed, Allah loves the good-doers", and the pardon is the overlooking of what they do, and the bearing with them is that they are not punished in haste, and the wording was given while the Prophet was among them and it was followed by the sword verse, and the love named at the end is for the one who does what is done with good grace, since the overlooking is itself the good that Allah loves, and the wisdom in it is that the Prophet of Islam abstains from doing what is otherwise quite natural when a people have wronged him, and the good grace in the pardon brings those who practise it closer to Him.

**Breaking the covenant, the condemnation and the hardened hearts.**

It means that it was because of their contravention of the solemn pledge that Allah made them far-removed from His mercy (that is, from its effects, which is the reality of 'La nah' or curse - Hadrat Thanavi) and made their hearts hardened against any penetration of truth. A pledge was taken from the Children of Israel by their prophet that they would lead a godly life, and twelve chiefs from their twelve tribes were appointed to keep a watch over them. The pledge taken from the Children of Israel was that they would make themselves godly by offering salat (prayers); that they would discharge the rights of others in the shape of zakat (obligatory alms-giving); align themselves on the side of God by supporting His prophets; and spend their assets in support of the struggle for the religion of God. Because of their breaking the promise that was taken from them, I distanced them from My mercy and I made their hearts so hard that no good could enter them and no advice could be of any benefit to them. (And because of their) i.e. the kings (breaking their covenant, We have cursed them) We punished them through imposing the capitation tax upon them (and made hard) and lightless (their hearts. They change words from their context) they change the traits and description of Muhammad ﷺ and the legal ruling on stoning [married people who fornicate] after this was exposited upon in the Torah (and forget a part) and leave part (of that whereof they were admonished) they were commanded with in the Torah concerning their following of Muhammad ﷺ and manifesting his traits and description to others. It means that the reason why they reject open verses of the Qur'an and all too manifest signs is that the stain of sins has settled down on their hearts.

**Distorting the words of the Scripture, and neglecting the Message sent to them.**

God says So because bi-mā the mā is extra of their breaking their covenant We cursed them We removed them from Our mercy and made their hearts hard unyielding to the acceptance of faith; they pervert words pertaining to the descriptions of Muhammad in the Torah and other things from their contexts those in which God has placed them in other words they substitute them; and they have forgotten they have abandoned a portion a part of what they were reminded of of what they were enjoined to in the Torah in the way of following Muhammad ; and you — addressing the Prophet s now — will never cease to discover some treachery on their part in the way of breaking a covenant or some other matter except for a few of them who have submitted themselves to Islam. They distort the placing of words by replacing them with other words, and by interpreting them according to their desires. (They change the words from their (right) places...) Since their comprehension became corrupt, they behaved treacherously with Allah's Ayat, altering His Book from its apparent meanings which He sent down, and distorting its indications. And their hearts became so hardened that they stooped to the level of 'moving words away from their places' which means that they alter the Word of God - in words or meanings or recitation - all of which have been described in the Holy Qur'an and the books of Alhadith, some of which have been acknowledged by European Christians as well (Tafsir Usmni). (but they have abandoned a good part of the Message that was sent to them. So We planted amongst them enmity and hatred till the Day of Resurrection;) They changed the words from their (right) places and have abandoned a good part of the Message that was sent to them.

**The deceit found on their part, except for a few.**

You will continuously discover, O Messenger, their betrayal of Allah and His believing servants, with the exception of a few of them, who fulfil the promise taken from them. A pledge was taken from the Children of Israel by their prophet that they would lead a godly life, and twelve chiefs from their twelve tribes were appointed to keep a watch over them. (Thou wilt not) O Muhammad (cease to discover treachery) and contravention (from all) i.e. the Banu Qurayzah (save a few of them) 'Abdullah Ibn Salam and his followers. God says So because bi-mā the mā is extra of their breaking their covenant We cursed them We removed them from Our mercy and made their hearts hard unyielding to the acceptance of faith; they pervert words pertaining to the descriptions of Muhammad in the Torah and other things from their contexts those in which God has placed them in other words they substitute them; and they have forgotten they have abandoned a portion a part of what they were reminded of of what they were enjoined to in the Torah in the way of following Muhammad ; and you — addressing the Prophet s now — will never cease to discover some treachery on their part in the way of breaking a covenant or some other matter except for a few of them who have submitted themselves to Islam.

**The command to pardon them, and the good it brings.**

Yet pardon them and forgive; surely God loves the virtuous this was abrogated by the ‘sword’ verse Q. 95. (But forgive them, and overlook (their misdeeds).) This, indeed, is the ultimate victory and triumph. Overlook what they do, because that is being good and Allah loves those who do good. It means that, despite their peculiar condition being what it is, it is better that the Prophet of Islam abstains from doing what is otherwise quite natural. Allah Almighty likes what is done with good grace - and it will definitely bring Muslims closer to Him. In other words, they concoct a religion of their own, keeping purely worldly considerations in view, and start calling it the religion of God. Because of their breaking the promise that was taken from them, I distanced them from My mercy and I made their hearts so hard that no good could enter them and no advice could be of any benefit to them.

14.text:
"And from those who say, “We are Christians,” We took their covenant" comes next, and the covenant taken from them is the same shape as the one taken from the Children of Israel, a promise in the Gospel that they should follow Muhammad and manifest his traits and not worship anyone except Allah or associate anyone with Him, and just as with the first group the verse names what they did with it: "but they neglected a portion of what they had been commanded to uphold", and the portion is what they left out of what they were commanded, the same kind of leaving their predecessors from among the Jews did. Then the answer comes in the words of the verse itself: "So We let hostility and enmity arise between them until the Day of Judgment", and the enmity is the killing and the destruction cast in the hearts between the groups, and the reading of the scene names the sects of Najran against each other, the Jacobites and the Marqusiyya and the Melkites, and the dissension is mutual, each one declaring the other to be a disbeliever, and the present scene bears out the same description, since a religion that is made up for oneself is bound to end in a sect gathering around it and fighting the next sect over it. "and soon Allah will inform them of all they have done" closes the verse, and the informing is about their handiwork, their opposition and treachery and concealment and enmity and hatred, and the repayment for the same is fixed to the Day named before it. The two punishments sit side by side in the passage, the one after the breaking of the first covenant and this one after the breaking of the second, and both are given in this world as a sign of the accounting that comes after it, and the one who reads the two punishments together reads the whole passage as one account of what a promise earns when it is broken and what the breaking brings into the world before the Hereafter, and the informing on that Day is of the very handiwork named here, and the handiwork is not hidden from the one it belongs to in this world either, since the enmity already answers it here and the accounting only makes it plain, and the warning in it is for the one who carries a promise now, since every promise in the passage is answered in this world before it is answered in the next, and the passage has now given both answers side by side.

**We took their covenant: what it contained.**

And with those who say ‘We are Christians’ this is semantically connected to what follows We made a covenant just as We did with the Children of Israel the Jews and they have forgotten a portion of that they were reminded of in the Gospel pertaining to faith and other matters and they too broke the covenant. (And with those who say: " Lo! we are Christians "), i.e. the Christians of Najran (We made a covenant) in the Gospel that they should follow Muhammad ﷺ and manifest his traits and not worship anyone or anything except Allah or associate anyone with Him, (but they forgot a part) they left part (of that whereof they were admonished) with which they were commanded. Just as I took a firm promise from the Jews, I also took a promise from those who declare themselves to be pure followers of Jesus ﷺ. When The People of the Book (i.e. those communities blessed with Divine Scriptures) go astray, they disregard the clear-cut, eternal parts of the Scriptures and hasten to embrace those parts which are of purely local or topical interest.

**What they left out of what they were commanded to uphold.**

They also left out practicing some of what they were advised to do, just as their predecessors from among the jews did. (And with those who say: " Lo! we are Christians "), i.e. the Christians of Najran (We made a covenant) in the Gospel that they should follow Muhammad ﷺ and manifest his traits and not worship anyone or anything except Allah or associate anyone with Him, (but they forgot a part) they left part (of that whereof they were admonished) with which they were commanded. They changed the words from their (right) places and have abandoned a good part of the Message that was sent to them.

**The hostility and enmity between them until the Day of Judgment.**

So We have stirred up We have caused among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection on account of their schisms and differing whims each sect charging the other with unbelief; and God will assuredly tell them in the Hereafter of what they wrought and requite them for this. (Therefore We have stirred up) We have cast (enmity) killing and destruction (and hatred) in the hearts (among them) between the Jews and Christians; and it is said between the Nestorians of Najran, the sects known as the Jacobites, the Marqusiyya and the Melkites (till the Day of Resurrection, when Allah will inform them of their handiwork) of their opposition, treachery, concealment, enmity and hatred. In this verse, the punishment described for Christians is mutual dissension. They start adopting a religion of their own imagining, casting aside their time-honoured authentic religion. Dissatisfied with the clear commandments given by God and His prophets on religious laws, spirituality and politics, they delve into them to find new points of contention. A stage comes when it will clearly be perpetuated until Doomsday, because man tends to treat the past as sacred, and once something is sanctified by time and tradition, it takes on an aura of being eternal. Verily, Allah loves the doers of good And from those who call themselves Christians, We took their covenant, but they have abandoned a good part of the Message that was sent to them.

**Soon Allah will inform them of all they have done.**

(Therefore We have stirred up) We have cast (enmity) killing and destruction (and hatred) in the hearts (among them) between the Jews and Christians; and it is said between the Nestorians of Najran, the sects known as the Jacobites, the Marqusiyya and the Melkites (till the Day of Resurrection, when Allah will inform them of their handiwork) of their opposition, treachery, concealment, enmity and hatred. (They change the words from their (right) places...) (but they have abandoned a good part of the Message that was sent to them. So We planted amongst them enmity and hatred till the Day of Resurrection;) From the first verse, 5:13, which dealt with the breach of trust by Jews and their punishment for it, we now move to the next verse, 5:14, which refers to Christians: ‌.

**The mutual dissension described for them.**

In this verse, the punishment described for Christians is mutual dissension. As for those who have moved away from their own religion turning into non-conformist, secular or atheistic individuals or groups, they are, for all practical purposes, out of the list of Christians - even though, they may count them as Christians among the nationalities of a country. If, among such people, that religious dissension and mutual hostility does not exist, it would not be contrary to this verse - because the conflict was based on religion, once the religion is not there, conflict too would not be there. 15.text:
"O People of the Book! Now Our Messenger has come to you" opens the verse on the same address the covenant passages used, and the two halves of the address sit in it together, the people named and the one who has come to them. What he comes with is then given in a single line: "revealing much of what you have hidden of the Scriptures and disregarding much", and the revealing is the making clear of what they used to conceal of the Scripture, the Torah and the Gospel, the traits and the description of the Prophet and the legal ruling on stoning as well as other things, and the disregarding is the pardoning of much of it, the leaving of many other things without mentioning them, because that would not be of any benefit and would serve only to disgrace those addressed. The two mistakes of the People of the Book sit on either side of this line, the first that they omitted some teachings by deliberate misinterpretation or distortion, and the second that they imposed upon themselves extra restrictions the law had never asked for, and the verse answers the first with the revealing and the second with the passing over. Then the last phrase: "There certainly has come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book", and the light is named in the readings as the Messenger himself and the Book is the Qur'an, lucid and plain and manifest, and the Book makes clear all of what people require for their worldly and religious affairs, and the lawful and the unlawful are the things it explains. The light and the Book are one arrival, so the one who sees the light and reads the Book is guided to the ways of peace, and that is where the next verse takes the thread, and the arrival named at the end of this verse is the same arrival the line before it described, the one who comes with the revealing and the passing over both in his hands, and both belong to the same arrival, the light and the clear Book that the next verse names.

**What the Messenger reveals of what they hide.**

O People of the Scripture Jews and Christians now there has come to you Our Messenger Muhammad making clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Scripture the Torah and the Gospel such as the ‘stoning’ verse and the description of the Prophet Muhammad and pardoning much of it which he does not reveal since this would not be of any benefit serving only to disgrace you. Now has come to you Our Messenger explaining to you much of that which you used to hide from the Scripture and passing over much. (O people of the Scripture!
